faq.a: Eesa is associated with the Arabic form عِيسَى, whose core sense is eesa; jesus (prophet).

faq.q: What is the origin of Eesa?
faq.a: Eesa is associated with Arabic. Eesa is Arabic عِيسَى (ʿĪsā), the Quranic form of Jesus.
Yes — the underlying form عِيسَى is Arabic.
Eesa can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Eesa should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. ʿĪsā is the Quranic Arabic form of Jesus and occurs in the Quran.

faq.q: What does Eesa mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Eesa is rendered عیسیٰ and carries the sense عیسیٰ، نبی کا نام.

faq.q: What does Eesa mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Eesa is rendered عیسی and carries the sense عیسی، نام پیامبر.
A romanized syllable approximation is ee-sa. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Eesa?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Eesa, eesa. Script forms are عيسى, عِيسَى, عیسی, عیسیٰ, ईसा.

faq.q: Is Eesa a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
